label: FP
reason: Both alerts are False Positives. For java/sql-injection (Alert 2, L56): the sink 'sql' uses 'bar' which resolves to constant 'moresafe' (when param!=null) or 'alsosafe' (when param==null) due to the list manipulation in doSomething(). For java/xss (Alert 1, L61-L62): the sink is the queryForObject call which receives 'sql', but 'bar' is always a constant string ('moresafe'/'alsosafe'), not user-controlled data.

evidence.note: doSomething() method manipulates user input into a list, removing index 0 then getting index 1, resulting in 'bar' always being constant 'moresafe' or 'alsosafe' regardless of user input
SQL injection sink - sql variable constructed from bar which is always a constant string
